chunks: He descended to the holy Najaf in the year [448] and he is the first who established the Hawza Ilmiyya there; to him belongs the credit for its establishment.
May God preserve it from evils and afflictions.

key_terms.النَّجَفِ الْأَشْرَفِ: Najaf al-Ashraf — the holy city in Iraq, site of Imam Ali's shrine and hub of Shia scholarship
key_terms.الْحَوْزَةَ الْعِلْمِيَّةَ: Hawza Ilmiyya — the Shia religious seminary/scholarly institution, founded by Shaykh al-Tusi
key_terms.الْفَضْلُ: merit, credit — the honour and distinction due for a foundational act

ai.seo_question: Who first established the Hawza Ilmiyya in Najaf al-Ashraf, and in what year?
ai.summary: This biographical note records that Shaykh al-Tusi (Shaykh al-Ta'ifa), the foremost Shia scholar of his era, relocated to Najaf al-Ashraf in 448 AH — following the destruction of his home and library in Baghdad — and there established the Hawza Ilmiyya, the institution of Shia religious learning that endures to the present day. The closing formula is an authorial supplication for the seminary's preservation.
